In one line

Sixty-five activity types feed one daily total in Vantage Fit, arriving three ways: automatic sync from Apple Health, Google Fit, Fitbit and Garmin, manual entry, or the phone camera. Steps, workouts and active minutes reconcile into a single number, so someone with only a phone competes on the same board as a watch owner.

Automatic sync

Steps and workouts flow in from Apple Health, Google Fit, Fitbit and Garmin, with more health data imported through Health Connect on Android.

Manual logging

No device for a session? Log it by hand. Great for a class, a swim or anything a tracker misses.

Camera tracking

The phone camera counts squats with pose detection and gives an awareness-level heart-rate check, not a medical-grade reading.

How the day adds up

Two rings, and steps that actually reconcile.

Sensible defaults

10,000 steps and 250 active calories a day when no challenge is running, adjustable per program.

Active minutes count movement that is not steps

Cycling or a workout earns active minutes, which convert at 100 steps a minute. The WHO's 150 minutes a week is a helpful yardstick, not a badge.

Honestly measured

A number you can stand behind.

A wellness program only works if the data is believable, so it counts what people actually did.

  • Duplicate days are caught

    A day that is a near-copy of the one before gets flagged, not counted twice.

  • Sync is rate-limited

    Updates are spaced on a minimum interval, so a flood of readings cannot inflate a total.

  • The same rules for everyone

    Phone-only or top-of-the-range watch, the count is measured the same way, so the leaderboard stays fair.

Questions before rollout

Before you trust the numbers

Rings, trends and custom activities live in the mobile app. Lite Mode plans track steps only.

Fitness & exerciseWellness leagues
Do employees need a fitness band?−
No. The phone is enough on its own, through its step counter, manual logging or the camera. A wearable is welcome, never required.
How does the step total add up?+
Three things add up: device steps, any manual steps your company allows, and active minutes converted at 100 steps a minute. One daily total.
How are duplicate or inflated steps handled?+
A day that looks like a near-copy of the one before is flagged, not counted twice. Sync is rate-limited too, so a burst of readings cannot inflate a total.
Is the camera heart-rate reading accurate?+
Awareness-level, a quick self-check, not a medical measurement. Anyone who wants precision connects a wearable.
Can we add our own activities?+
Yes. Admins can add branded loggable activities like "Office Yoga" and habit activities like "Avoid Sugar," self-serve, no developer needed.
